description: Explicit-boundary mappings for hydrogen, advanced generation, carbon management, marine energy, and long-duration storage.

doe-commercial-liftoff.title: U.S. DOE Pathways to Commercial Liftoff
doe-commercial-liftoff.license: U.S. Government work; verify report-specific third-party notices
doe-commercial-liftoff.applicable_boundary: Technology-family taxonomy and commercialization context for clean hydrogen, advanced nuclear, carbon management, geothermal, and long-duration storage
doe-commercial-liftoff.note: The source supports technology classification only. No cost or performance projections are bundled.

nrel-annual-technology-baseline.title: NREL Annual Technology Baseline
nrel-annual-technology-baseline.license: U.S. Government work; verify dataset terms
nrel-annual-technology-baseline.note: This pack contains names and boundaries, not ATB numerical values.

doe-liquid-alkaline-electrolysis-targets.title: U.S. DOE: Technical Targets for Liquid Alkaline Electrolysis
doe-liquid-alkaline-electrolysis-targets.license: U.S. Government work; verify page-specific third-party notices
doe-liquid-alkaline-electrolysis-targets.applicable_boundary: Low-temperature liquid alkaline electrolyzer system electricity to hydrogen energy on an LHV basis
doe-liquid-alkaline-electrolysis-targets.note: The published 2022 status and future targets form a scenario envelope, not an empirical uncertainty distribution.

nrel-integrated-heat-pump-thermal-storag.title: NREL/TP-5700-79806: Integrated Heat Pump Thermal Storage and Comparison with Other Energy Storage Systems
nrel-integrated-heat-pump-thermal-storag.license: U.S. Government work; verify report-specific third-party notices
nrel-integrated-heat-pump-thermal-storag.applicable_boundary: Round-trip electrical efficiency cases for pumped-thermal and electrochemical storage technologies tabulated in the report
nrel-integrated-heat-pump-thermal-storag.note: The table combines literature cases with different technologies, durations, and power ratings; each prior below narrows its applicability.

doe-aem-electrolysis-analysis-2022.title: DOE Hydrogen Production Cost and Performance Analysis
doe-aem-electrolysis-analysis-2022.license: U.S. Government work; annual merit review presentation
doe-aem-electrolysis-analysis-2022.applicable_boundary: AEM electrolyzer system electricity to hydrogen production for modeled pure-water and KOH cases
doe-aem-electrolysis-analysis-2022.note: Near-term modeled system electricity is 66.1 kWh/kg H2 for pure water and 50.8 for 1 M KOH; future cases are 45.3 and 42.9. These are scenarios, not field measurements.

doe-fuel-cell-comparison.title: U.S. DOE Comparison of Fuel Cell Technologies
doe-fuel-cell-comparison.license: U.S. Government work; verify page-specific third-party notices
doe-fuel-cell-comparison.applicable_boundary: Fuel LHV input to electrical output for fuel-cell technology families
doe-fuel-cell-comparison.note: DOE lists 60% LHV electrical efficiency for solid-oxide fuel cells; it is a technology-family value, not a specific product guarantee.

doe-mit-geothermal-conversion-2006.title: DOE-sponsored MIT Future of Geothermal Energy, Chapter 3 conversion assumptions
doe-mit-geothermal-conversion-2006.license: Public DOE-sponsored report; verify report-specific notices
doe-mit-geothermal-conversion-2006.applicable_boundary: Produced geothermal heat delivered to a binary or flash power cycle to net electricity
doe-mit-geothermal-conversion-2006.note: Table 3.1 gives net thermal efficiencies of 11%, 14%, 16%, 18%, and 22% at 150, 200, 250, 300, and 350 C. Ambient conditions and conversion cycle are embedded assumptions.

nrc-nuscale-us600.title: U.S. NRC Design Certification - NuScale US600
nrc-nuscale-us600.license: U.S. Government work; applicant design information may retain separate rights
nrc-nuscale-us600.applicable_boundary: Certified NuScale module rated reactor thermal output to rated electrical output
nrc-nuscale-us600.note: Each module is reported as 160 MWt and 50 MWe, giving a rated ratio of 31.25%; this is one design, not the full SMR family.

inl-microreactor-program-2025.title: Idaho National Laboratory Microreactor Program Review: Demonstration Capabilities Overview
inl-microreactor-program-2025.license: U.S. Government-sponsored laboratory presentation; verify third-party design notices
inl-microreactor-program-2025.applicable_boundary: Selected developer-reported microreactor thermal output to electrical output
inl-microreactor-program-2025.note: Public design pairs include 5/15, 17/50, and 50/112 MWe/MWth; many concepts do not publish both values.

doe-sco2-power-cycle.title: U.S. DOE Supercritical CO2 Power Cycles program pages
doe-sco2-power-cycle.license: U.S. Government work; verify page-specific third-party notices
doe-sco2-power-cycle.applicable_boundary: High-temperature heat supplied to an indirectly heated supercritical CO2 power cycle to electricity
doe-sco2-power-cycle.note: DOE states greater than 50% is possible and describes it as a demonstration pathway, not established commercial fleet performance.

doe-storage-cost-performance-2022.title: DOE Energy Storage Grand Challenge Cost and Performance Assessment 2022
doe-storage-cost-performance-2022.license: U.S. Government work; PNNL technical report
doe-storage-cost-performance-2022.applicable_boundary: Electricity at grid connection during charge to electricity returned at grid connection over a complete storage cycle
doe-storage-cost-performance-2022.note: The assessment uses 52% RTE for CAES and reports an 80%-90% composite gravitational-storage range with average values dependent on power.

doe-csp-power-block-rd.title: U.S. DOE Power Block R&D for Concentrating Solar-Thermal Power Systems
doe-csp-power-block-rd.license: U.S. Government work; verify page-specific third-party notices
doe-csp-power-block-rd.applicable_boundary: Thermal energy delivered to a concentrating-solar power block to gross electricity
doe-csp-power-block-rd.note: DOE reports approximately 35%-45% thermal-to-electric efficiency for existing steam-Rankine power blocks and describes higher values as research targets. Solar collection, receiver, storage, and net auxiliary losses are outside this boundary.

carrier.boundary: Minimum separation work rather than actual capture energy
